Header: Erwinia spp. Sinhala: Bacterianu kesel ala kunuwima, Tamil: Vaalai Kilanku Aluhal

Prevention: Select non-infected fields based on field history.
Prepre the land properly with ample drainage system.
Use healthy planting materials obtained from non-infected cultivation or tissue culture for new cultivation.
Remove and destroy crop debris before cultivation and just after harvesting.
Avoid damage to rhizomes and prevent pests such as
Rhizome weevil as the bacteria can infect through wounds.
Monitoring: Wilting and dying of newly planted suckers.
Splitting of the pseudostems at the base.
Dark brown rotting starting from the periphery of the rhizome extends towards central core.
Rotting progressing upwards in the pseudostem, destroying leaf bases.
Unpleasant odour associated with rotted tissues.
Infected plants which can easily be pulled out at the rotted collar region or are highly vulnerable to toppling over due to wind.
Direct Control: Pull out infected plants along with rhizomes and roots and destroy by deep burying or burning.
Avoid water movement from infected plants to healthy plants.
No chemical control for this disease.
